papers.title: AnySleep: a channel-agnostic deep learning system for high-resolution sleep staging in multi-center cohorts.
papers.summary: Developed AnySleep, a channel-agnostic deep neural network trained on over 20,000 overnight EEG/EOG recordings from 28 datasets to perform sleep staging at adjustable temporal resolutions. The model achieved state-of-the-art 30-s epoch performance, remained robust with limited channels, and at sub-30-s resolution improved prediction of obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy type 1, and insomnia compared to 30-s scoring.

papers.title: An automated EEG-ECG framework for CAP-HRV analysis: enabling brain-heart coupling studies in sleep disorders.
papers.summary: Presented an open-source MATLAB framework integrating rule-based cyclic alternating pattern (CAP) A1 detection from EEG with heart rate variability (HRV) feature extraction from ECG within a time-synchronized workflow, using validated PhysioZoo/mhrv routines. A worked example on OSAD+ patients (n=18) and a healthy reference dataset (15 controls, 785 A1 epochs) demonstrated synchronized CAP-HRV output to facilitate brain-heart coupling research in sleep disorders.

papers.title: EEG-Based Cognitive Overload-Driven Adaptive Training for Enhancing Performance Under Simulated High-Stress Space Operation Tasks.
papers.summary: Proposes an EEG-based cognitive overload-driven adaptive training method combining hybrid feature selection, NFDTW-based feature alignment, and a shared knowledge layer, with a dual-factor task regulation strategy adjusting difficulty by performance and overload state. Achieved online overload detection accuracies of 92.07% and 84.67% on two datasets (up to 8.34% relative improvement) and, in a VR robotic arm docking task, the adaptive group showed significant gains in task performance and SAS versus fixed and control groups.

papers.title: Characterization of Sleep, Spectral, and Epileptiform Activity in Individuals Aged 8-27 Years with SYNGAP1-Related Disorder Using an at-Home Dry EEG Headband
papers.summary: Using an at-home dry-electrode EEG headband, the study collected 180 multi-night recordings (23 participants) in SYNGAP1-related disorder and found interictal epileptiform discharges in 22 of 23 participants without electrographic seizures, plus increased wake after sleep onset, reduced sleep efficiency, altered N1/N2/N3 staging, and elevated broadband power with reduced relative alpha power and alpha-theta ratio; spectral differences were tightly sleep-stage dependent.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Machine Learning for Biosignal Applications - A Review.
papers.summary: Systematically reviewed 53 papers on uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods for machine learning applied to biosignals such as EEG, ECG, EOG, and EMG. The review catalogued methods, evaluation measures, theoretical frameworks, and misconceptions, concluding that promising UQ approaches exist but that research on human-system interaction with uncertainty models in clinical settings is still needed.

papers.title: Longitudinal persistence of EEG brain fingerprints:phase and complex coherency geometry across sessions andfunctional states
papers.summary: Investigated the longitudinal persistence of EEG connectivity-based individual fingerprints using phase and complex coherency geometry across three cohorts spanning one month to five years, without a trained identity classifier. Alpha phasors identified 81.67% (RestCog) and 79.55% (L-FAME) of participants in rest-to-rest matching, and after five years 77.67% rank-1 identification was retained, while state changes (eyes-open/closed, task) weakened identification, distinguishing temporal persistence from robustness across functional states.

papers.title: Capturing Class Differences in EEG Connectivity with Class-discriminative Multivariate IMagInary Coherency (CMIMIC).
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: Introduced Class-discriminative Multivariate ImagInary Coherency (CMIMIC), a multivariate method that maximizes differences in imaginary coherency between two classes to identify condition-specific EEG/MEG functional connectivity. In simulations and resting-state EEG, CMIMIC outperformed traditional imaginary coherence across classifiers and conditions, identified a stable core of informative sources, and provided spatially interpretable source configurations.

papers.title: Quantifying Interictal Spike Asymmetry on Scalp EEG to Lateralize the Seizure-Onset Zone in Temporal Lobe Epilepsy.
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort study (365 drug-resistant TLE patients) quantifying automatically detected interictal spike rate asymmetry on scalp EEG with a deep learning model and leave-one-hemisphere-out lateralization to predict clinician-annotated seizure focus. Left-vs-right/bilateral classification reached AUC 0.78 (70% accuracy) and right-vs-left/bilateral AUC 0.80 (75% accuracy); model-surgery concordance was associated with favorable Engel I outcomes.

papers.title: Multidimensional EEG Feature Fusion and Interpretable Machine Learning for Identifying Cognitive Impairment in Depression.
papers.summary: Developed an interpretable subject-level machine learning framework using resting-state EEG features (phase lag index, relative power, fuzzy entropy across five bands) to identify cognitive impairment in 142 patients with depression. The final model achieved 80.39% accuracy and 83.74% AUC, with discriminative features concentrated in beta1 and beta2 bands reflecting altered phase synchronization, oscillatory activity, and signal complexity.

papers.title: A self-supervised reconstruction framework for segment-level detection of task-induced deviations in multi-channel EEG.
papers.summary: Developed a self-supervised deep learning framework using a hierarchical variational auto-encoder to detect segment-level EEG anomalies during mental arithmetic from resting-state training data. Outlier segments showed distinct temporal and spectral features in delta, theta, and beta bands, localized mainly to peripheral electrodes, and co-occurrence analysis revealed dynamic spatial patterns.

papers.title: Measuring Sleep at Home in Adolescents With Autism Using EEG Headbands: Protocol for a Remote Study.
papers.summary: Presents a remote study protocol using wearable EEG headbands to monitor sleep at home in adolescents with autism spectrum disorder and typically developing peers, including a desensitization protocol for sensory sensitivities. The study aimed to test thalamocortical circuit dysfunction in autism via sleep oscillations; 146 participants completed data collection, and analysis is underway.

papers.title: Predictive value of EEG/ECG biomarkers for treatment response in depression.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Retrospectively analyzed 153 adults with depressive episodes and found that treatments concordant with individualized resting-state EEG/ECG biomarker reports had higher response rates than non-concordant treatments (46% vs 26%; NNT ≈5) across ECT, rTMS, (es)ketamine, and SSRIs. The authors conclude EEG/ECG-based decision support may improve antidepressant treatment response but requires prospective confirmation.

papers.title: EEG Feature-level integration for robust command generation in SSVEP-based brain-computer interfaces.
papers.summary: Developed an EEG feature-level integration strategy combining correlation and alpha-rhythm features to detect SSVEP Blocking Response, improving precision, recall, and specificity by 17.11%, 8.50%, and 5.44% over a prior SSVEP-BR detection framework. An asynchronous BCI using this approach generated 8 commands from two stimulation frequencies and controlled a robotic arm online.

papers.title: Mental replay rescales the subjective duration of past events via alpha and theta oscillations
papers.summary: Investigated whether mentally replaying past events at different speeds alters their perceived duration, using EEG during replay of naturalistic videos. Expanded replay lengthened duration judgments relative to free and compressed replay without affecting memory content; alpha and theta power interacted with replay speed to predict reported duration, suggesting duration is reconstructed via oscillatory dynamics rather than read out from retrieved content.

papers.title: Flavonoid chronotherapy normalizes circadian dynamics and sleep architecture in mice with painful nerve injury
papers.summary: In spared nerve injury PER2::LUC mice with wireless EEG/EMG, showed that nerve injury increased Per2 rhythm amplitude in dorsal root ganglia and disrupted sleep, while continuous nobiletin or tangeretin restored Per2 rhythms, alleviated dynamic hypersensitivity on post-surgical day 14, and tangeretin improved NREM sleep and wakefulness disturbances.

papers.title: Bridging Sensory Extraction and Decision Dynamics: Face Pareidolia Emergent from Bottom-Up and Top-Down Interactions
papers.summary: Recorded EEG while participants viewed object-to-face morphs to investigate whether face pareidolia arises from bottom-up or top-down processes. Early occipitotemporal areas tracked physical features linearly, while later frontocentral channels showed sigmoidal categorical decisions; unambiguous stimuli were resolved via feedforward flow, whereas ambiguous pareidolic images recruited prolonged top-down feedback, with animacy priors biasing decisions.

papers.title: Early movement intention recognition via corticomuscular synchrony in complex tasks.
papers.summary: Using wavelet transform coherence on EEG-EMG from 12 healthy volunteers performing robotic-arm reaching tasks, identified significant pre-motor corticomuscular desynchronization 100–200 ms before EMG onset, and a CMC phase-dynamics classifier outperformed EEG power spectral density, reaching mean accuracy 0.80 with peak intention classification near 100 ms pre-EMG.

papers.title: Wavelets and switching in bistable visual perception: Comment on "Wavelet analysis in biomedical research: A versatile tool for multiscale signal characterization and functional connectivity analysis" by Kralj et al․.
papers.summary: This comment argues that bistable visual perception links wavelet-based signal characterization to functional connectivity, proposing that integrating time-local dominance estimates with dynamic connectivity could clarify network reconfiguration during perceptual switching, while cautioning that frequency tags are indirect perceptual markers and require behavioral validation.

papers.title: Differential circadian time modulates of dentate gyrus and CA1 excitation-inhibition balance and seizure threshold.
papers.summary: Using video-EEG, optogenetic seizure induction, mRNA sequencing, and patch-clamp recording in mice, this study showed that circadian time differentially modulates seizure thresholds and excitation-inhibition balance in hippocampal dentate gyrus versus CA1, with CA1 diurnal-nocturnal seizure threshold patterns matching systemic pilocarpine-induced seizures.

papers.title: Outcome-Blind EEG Microstate Topography After Cardiac Arrest: Spatial Expression of a Lateralized Microstate and Association with Neurological Outcome.
papers.summary: In an outcome-blind secondary analysis of the multicenter I-CARE/PhysioNet database (567 comatose cardiac arrest survivors), microstate decomposition froze a four-state solution, and M2 global explained variance (GEV) was higher with favorable outcome (median 0.0852 vs 0.0564) and inversely associated with CPC severity, with adjusted OR 1.30 per 1-SD increase; standalone ROC AUC was 0.59.

papers.title: E-MDD: an evidence-guided explainable framework for EEG-based depression recognition.
papers.summary: Developed E-MDD, a three-stage framework fusing EEG latent features with neurophysiological biomarkers and using a large language model to generate evidence-guided textual explanations for depression recognition, achieving AUC 0.8472 and F1-score 0.8421 on the Mumtaz dataset with faithful explanations replicated across EEGNet and EEGConformer.

papers.title: Processed electroencephalogram-guided anesthesia and its impact on postoperative delirium and perioperative efficiency: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 87 RCTs (30,611 patients) found that processed EEG-guided anesthesia reduced propofol and volatile anesthetic use, lowered postoperative delirium risk by 27%, and shortened extubation, wake-up, orientation, and PACU times, with strongest evidence for BIS monitoring.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Alpha-Band Oscillations as Potential Indicators of Executive Subcomponents Dysfunction correlating to the Severity of Cerebral Small Vessel Disease.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional analysis of 181 patients with cerebral small vessel disease, resting-state EEG alpha-band parameters, especially occipital peak frequency, were associated with inhibitory control measures but showed no robust association with working memory, with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.80 for the best inhibitory-control model.

papers.title: Concordance between magnetoencephalography and intracranial EEG and association with surgical outcomes in MRI-negative epilepsy.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 51 MRI-negative drug-resistant epilepsy patients, MEG localized interictal abnormalities in 65%, and among 32 with localizing MEG and an iEEG-defined seizure-onset zone, 72% showed complete lobar-level concordance; 1-year Engel class I outcomes occurred in 91% with complete concordance versus 63% of MEG-negative patients.

papers.title: A multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset with repeated experience sampling
papers.summary: This paper presents a BIDS-formatted multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset from 24 healthy adults with carbon wire loop artifact sensors, continuous performance task responses, experience sampling of 13 thought dimensions (468 ratings per participant), and mental health surveys across two days (~1.33 hours of simultaneous data per person).

papers.title: Tetradic Dynamics of Dyadic Sensorimotor Coordination: A Multiscale EEG Hyperscanning Study
papers.summary: This dual-brain EEG hyperscanning study examined leader-follower sensorimotor coordination in healthy adult pairs using a 2x2 design crossing Role with Mirroring versus Matching, proposing a tetradic framework for dyadic interaction. Neural analyses showed greater tonic power and phasic clusters during Matching, role-dependent anticipatory and post-response patterns, and information-theoretic signatures separating Leader-weighted predictive information from Follower-specific adaptive information, with sparse Synergy and Redundancy across specific cortical regions.

papers.title: Improved Sleep and Clinical Outcomes Following a Single-Session Intervention among Adolescents with Borderline Personality Disorder Features
papers.summary: In a single-session sleep-focused intervention trial (NCT04507308) with 57 adolescents aged 13-18 having 3+ impairing borderline personality disorder features, objective at-home EEG and subjective/EMA measures showed improved sleep quantity and quality, earlier sleep onset and waketime, fewer awakenings, and improvements in multiple BPD symptom indices maintained at one-month follow-up.

papers.title: A non-randomized trial of the effects of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on cognitive performance and resting state connectivity.
papers.summary: In a non-randomized trial of 40 healthy adults, active versus sham transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation was associated with improved BrainHQ cognitive-training performance and decreased frontal-central-parietal delta-band EEG connectivity, with delta connectivity during stimulation positively related to mood improvement; executive function tasks showed no group difference and effects did not survive multiple-comparison correction.

papers.title: Naturalistic language assessment and brain-network biomarkers in post-stroke aphasia for precision neurorehabilitation.
papers.summary: Integrative review synthesizing evidence on naturalistic language assessment, portable neuroimaging (EEG/fNIRS), and brain-network biomarkers in post-stroke aphasia, proposing an operational ecological biomarker framework linking connected-speech features, neural measures, and longitudinal outcomes for precision neurorehabilitation.

papers.title: EEG decodability of facial expressions and their stereoscopic depth cues in immersive virtual reality
papers.summary: Combined immersive VR, EEG, and eye tracking in 34 participants to show that time-resolved multivariate decoding reliably differentiates facial expressions and detects a distinct neural signature of stereoscopic depth cues, while expression decoding remained invariant across depth conditions.

papers.title: Depth-adaptive suppression of subject-dependent interference for robust cross-subject EEG emotion recognition.
papers.summary: Proposed a two-stage layer-adaptive framework built on EEG Conformer that uses differentiable gates and adversarial subject classifiers to locate and suppress subject-specific interference, plus a subject-aware supervised contrastive regularizer, improving cross-subject EEG emotion recognition under leave-one-subject-out evaluation on SEED and SEED-IV.

papers.title: Improvement in naming with tDCS and alteration of functional connectivity in post-stroke aphasia: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a double-blind sham-controlled randomized trial of 60 post-stroke aphasia patients, anodal tDCS over the left Sylvian parietal temporal region plus speech-language therapy for four weeks produced significantly greater improvements in picture naming and auditory word-picture identification than sham (p < 0.001). EEG cross-approximate entropy showed increased functional connectivity across multiple left-hemisphere and bilateral temporal electrode pairs after tDCS.

papers.title: An Exceptional Mobility Group Among Older Adults: Protocol for the Super Movers Study.
papers.summary: This protocol describes the Super Movers Study, which aims to enroll 350 adults aged 65 and older, classify them by gait speed into fast, usual, and slow movers, and assess brain imaging, mobile EEG during walking, multisensory integration, blood biomarkers, aging clocks, and cognition to identify substrates predicting cognitive and physical decline.

papers.title: General information reliability, perceived educational quality, and transparency of YouTube videos on epileptiform discharges: an exploratory cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study rated 25 English-language YouTube videos on epileptiform discharges using DISCERN, the Global Quality Scale, and JAMA criteria, finding moderate-to-good average perceived educational quality and information reliability but limited transparency (mean JAMA 1.98). The authors emphasize that the instruments are not EEG-specific and the findings are exploratory, without assessment of EEG accuracy or learner outcomes.

papers.title: Functional brain activity in cancer-related cognitive impairment: a scoping review of EEG studies.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-ScR scoping review mapped 60 EEG studies of cognitive functioning in people with cancer, finding that task-based event-related potentials (especially oddball and attention tasks) predominated over quantitative EEG, with longer P300 latency and lower amplitude common in non-CNS cancers but inconsistent and often untested associations with cognitive outcomes. The authors conclude the evidence is methodologically heterogeneous and call for larger longitudinal studies with consistent cognitive measures.

papers.title: Assessment of Compliance With the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence Guidance in the Management of Patients Referred Following a First Suspected Seizure: A Retrospective Clinical Audit.
papers.summary: Retrospective clinical audit of 53 patients referred to a first-seizure clinic, assessing adherence to NICE guidance on specialist assessment, ECG, EEG, neuroimaging, recurrence-risk assessment, and safety advice. Compliance was high for ECG (100%), recurrence-risk documentation (100%), and safety-netting/driving advice (100%), but only 9.4% had specialist assessment within two weeks and EEG was markedly delayed (mean ~12.5 weeks), identifying timely EEG access as the largest gap.

papers.title: An integrated PCA-XGBoost method for fluorescence spectral analysis of marine microplastics.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.summary: The paper proposes an interpretable PCA-XGBoost framework for fluorescence spectral analysis of microplastics, linking PCA loading profiles with XGBoost feature importance to identify characteristic wavelengths, and reports 99.94% overall classification accuracy across pure and mixed, aged and unaged polymer samples with application to real marine microplastics.

papers.title: Three repeated intrathecal injections of allogenic umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stromal cells in autism spectrum disorder: a Phase I clinical trial.
papers.summary: Phase I open-label trial testing three repeated intrathecal injections of allogeneic umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (20×10⁶ per dose at one-month intervals) in five children with autism spectrum disorder. Treatment was safe and well-tolerated with no serious adverse events; exploratory behavioral improvements on CARS were seen in all children and CSF TNF-α and IL-6 levels consistently decreased, supporting immunomodulatory effects and warranting larger controlled trials.

papers.title: Electrophysiology Team-Administered Conscious Sedation for Pulsed-Field Versus Radiofrequency Ablation in Atrial Fibrillation.
papers.summary: Randomized 1:1 trial in 120 patients with symptomatic drug-refractory atrial fibrillation comparing electrophysiology team-administered conscious sedation for pulsed-field ablation versus radiofrequency ablation, assessing tolerance, procedural efficiency, and safety. PFA showed lower FPS-R pain scores and shorter total procedure and left atrial dwell times, with higher cough incidence during pulmonary vein isolation (21.7% vs 6.7%) but no serious sedation-related complications, supporting feasibility of EP team-administered conscious sedation for PFA in selected low-risk patients.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
